newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico monetary policy still tight -Morgan Stanley.
newsitem.headline: Mexico monetary policy still tight -Morgan Stanley.

text.p: Slightly greater than expected growth in Mexico's monetary base does not signal a looser monetary policy, Morgan Stanley economist Ernest "Chip" Brown said on Tuesday.
"I don't think the growth in the base has been much of a problem at all. If anything it is still slightly restrictive," he said in a telephone interview.

He added in a report released Tuesday that monetary base growth of 27 percent over the past 12 months has been restrictive, given 24.5 percent inflation and an estimated 6.5 percent growth during the same 12-month period.
"Higher-than-expected money demand with a low and stable budget deficit, we feel, is more indicative of stronger growth and more capital inflows than higher inflation," he wrote.
Morgan Stanley has recently increased its growth estimate for the year to 4.3 percent from 4.0 percent and lowered its inflation estimate to 17 percent from 19 percent.
Growth in the monetary base became an issue after it exceeded Banco de Mexico's daily projections earlier this year.
